prompt: Pick one constructor out of four by its exact parameter types and build an object with it, then report which arities a class offers. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: getDeclaredConstructor performs an exact signature match, so the Class objects you hand it must be the declared parameter types, not the types of the values you intend to pass. For primitives that means int.class and double.class -- the wrapper classes Integer.class and Double.class describe different types and will not match, which is the single most common reflection bug. Once the Constructor is in hand, setAccessible(true) makes even a package-private or private constructor usable, and newInstance spreads your Object[] across the parameters, boxing and unboxing as needed. Catching NoSuchMethodException and returning null turns a missing signature into an ordinary answer instead of a crash.
hints: Wrap only the getDeclaredConstructor call in a try/catch for NoSuchMethodException; returning null there is what the Javadoc asks for.
constructor.newInstance(args) takes varargs, so passing the Object[] straight through spreads it across the parameters -- an empty array works for the no-argument constructor.
For arities, getDeclaredConstructors() (plural, no arguments) gives you the whole array; collect getParameterCount() from each and finish with Collections.sort.
